title: Yuki’s snow festival diary
text:
Friday 6 February

Today our class went to Odori Park in Sapporo to see the Snow Festival, and my toes are still tingling. Mr Kato made us wear two pairs of socks. I thought that was silly until we stepped outside. The air was so cold that it made my nose ache.

I did not expect the snow sculptures to be so enormous. One was a castle taller than a bus. Workers had carved tiny windows and winding staircases into it, and I counted four chimneys. After dark, coloured lights shone on it, and it looked as if the castle had been made from sugar. I wanted to stay all night, but the bus was waiting.

Saturday 7 February

I went back with Dad and my little sister, Aoi. She complained all through the queue for hot corn soup because she was hungry and her gloves were wet. Then she took one sip and was smiling again. Dad says the soup is so good because everything tastes better when you are cold.

Afterwards we built a small snow rabbit beside the path. It had pebble eyes and ears made from two flat pieces of bark. In the afternoon the sun came out and the rabbit began to lose its nose. I felt a little sad, but Dad only shrugged. "That is what snow art is," he said. "You enjoy it while it is here."

Sunday 8 February

It was our last day at the festival. We watched the sculptors work on an ice slide, and I fell down it twice and loved it both times. On the train home I was thinking about Dad's words. Perhaps the sculptors do not mind that their work will melt. They know that everyone who sees it will remember it.

Next year I am going to ask if I can help to build something. Even if it is only a rabbit.
